commands.name: run
commands.summary: Mutate the package and run its tests against each mutant
commands.detail: dir is the package's directory, here unless given; in a workspace, a member's. The run passes when the score reaches the threshold, or with --fail-on-new when every mutant no test catches is in the baseline. A full run, one without --only, writes report files, and offers the commands to work on each missed mutant. Its progress goes to stderr, so stdout holds only the result. --shard runs one share of the mutants, for splitting a run across CI jobs, and --from-shards puts the shares back together as the whole run.
commands.exits: 0 when the score reaches the threshold, 1 when it doesn't; with --fail-on-new, 0 when every mutant no test catches is in the baseline, 1 when one isn't.

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: Run mutants' tests: it passes when they catch every one not skipped
commands.detail: How a fix is proved: each missed mutant offers it as "done when", and a card with several mutants names them all, split by commas; spaces split them too, and the directory comes after them. An id names its mutant whatever options showed it, so verify needs no --operators or --unsafe to find one.
commands.exits: 0 when it catches each mutant named, or the mutant is skipped or crashed where a crash proves nothing; 1 while one is still missed or not covered.

examples.cargo: cargo mutastic verify mb2f8ae57 m95f96847 fixtures/pricing

commands.name: explain
commands.summary: Everything known of one mutant, with its tests run
commands.detail: Its card when it's missed, or what became of it otherwise, then what the change is, its operator, how its id is made, where it is, and how the last run of every mutant, by run or next, went for it, from that run's mutation.json.
commands.exits: 0 whatever the mutant's result: it explains, it doesn't judge.

commands.name: ignore
commands.summary: Record a decision not to test one mutant
commands.detail: It goes in .mutastic/ignores.yaml in the package's directory with its line and the reason, to commit and review, and lapses when that line changes: the mutant runs again, and run-finished lists it in staleIgnores. --remove takes one back; ignore --prune takes away every one that has lapsed. --propose records it in .mutastic/proposals.yaml instead, for a person to accept with --accept: how a coding agent says a mutant isn't worth a test, since until then it still counts as missed. A proposal that a mutant is equivalent or unreachable says the one case where it differs, and why that can't happen. It runs no tests, and each step says how to undo it.
commands.exits: 0 when the decision is recorded, proposed, accepted or removed; 1 when --accept names a mutant that isn't proposed, or --remove one that isn't ignored.

examples.commandLine: mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --reason="totals are rounded to tens"
examples.cargo: cargo mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --reason="totals are rounded to tens"

examples.commandLine: mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --propose --as=unreachable --reason="Differs only when total is 100. That can't happen because prices end in 9."
examples.cargo: cargo mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --propose --as=unreachable --reason="Differs only when total is 100. That can't happen because prices end in 9."

commands.name: next
commands.summary: Show the missed mutant most worth a test first, and why
commands.detail: The missed mutants as a queue, one line's at a time, in the order a run ranks them: its card, why it's first, and the command that says when it's done. --top shows the first few, spread over the code. With a baseline, new misses come before the baseline's. While the code under test is the same, it runs only the mutants the last next left uncaught, so any a new test catches drop out; once that code changes, it runs every mutant again. A mutant proposed for ignoring isn't queued: it waits on a person. For an agent, one task, and to run next again after it.
commands.exits: 0 when nothing missed is left, or only mutants proposed for ignoring; 1 while something is queued.

commands.name: baseline
commands.summary: Record every mutant missed now, so later misses are told from them
commands.detail: Runs the mutants and writes each one missed or not covered, by id, to .mutastic/baseline.yaml in the package's directory, to commit. From then on a miss that isn't in it is new: gate holds only new misses, next offers them first, and run --fail-on-new fails only on them. It's never rewritten to take in new misses: --prune runs the mutants and drops the baseline's that are caught now.
commands.exits: 0 when the baseline is written or pruned; 1 when there's one already and --prune isn't given, or --prune is given and there's none.

commands.name: gate open
commands.summary: Start gating a coding agent's task: keep where it starts
commands.detail: Keeps the commit the task starts from, its ignores, and how many tests run and are ignored, in target/mutastic, so gate check can say whether the task is done. With --hook, once for each of the agent's sessions; at a later prompt, it takes in the ignores made since the agent stopped.
commands.exits: 0 once it has kept where the task starts; 2 outside a git repository with a commit.

commands.name: gate check
commands.summary: Say whether a gated task is done: its changed lines' mutants caught
commands.detail: Runs the tests and the mutants on the lines changed since gate open: the tests run even with no mutant on those lines, and only a task that changed nothing skips them. The task is done when the tests pass, each mutant is caught or proposed for a person to ignore, no ignore was made by the task, and no test was taken away or ignored; until then it says what's left, as the agent format does. With --hook it answers as the agent's hook, and lets the agent stop, saying what's left, when it changed nothing since it was sent back, or after --tries.
commands.exits: 0 when the task is done, 1 when it isn't, 2 when no task is open. With --hook, 0 either way: the answer is what it prints, a block or a message, as the agent's hooks read it, and with nothing open the agent may stop.

commands.name: gate close
commands.summary: Stop gating a task: forget where it started
commands.detail: The next gate open starts a new task.
commands.exits: 0 whether a task was open or not: it says which, or with --hook says nothing.

commands.name: mutants
commands.summary: List the mutants, without building or running anything
commands.detail: One line each: its id, place, operator, the change, and the function it's in. A mutant near unsafe code says why it's marked, and the last lines count what was left out. With --operators and --unsafe, it shows what those would add before a run.

options.name: --threshold
options.help: The score a run must reach to pass; 80 unless set

options.name: --fail-on-new
options.help: Pass when every mutant no test catches is in .mutastic/baseline.yaml, and fail on one that isn't, whatever the score: the threshold isn't applied. For a package whose score can't reach it yet; mutastic baseline writes the file

options.name: --since
options.help: Mutate only the lines changed since the merge-base of HEAD and REF, uncommitted and new files included; the default branch without one. With no mutant on those lines, nothing is built or run

options.name: --only
options.help: Run one mutant, or several split by commas, whatever --operators says

options.name: --workers
options.help: How many mutants run side by side; half the cores, from 1 to 4, unless set

options.name: --no-suggestions
options.help: Don't look for a test that catches each missed mutant, which runs the missed mutant's function outside the tests

options.name: --force-coverage
options.help: Build and run every test even when no mutant is there to run, to check or time the suite

options.name: --operators
options.help: Which operators run: a set (defaults, stronger or extended), or operator ids split by commas, in place of mutastic.yaml's operators; defaults unless set

options.name: --unsafe
options.help: Which unsafe code is mutated: skip leaves unsafe code and the functions holding an unsafe block alone, enclosing mutates those functions too, all unsafe code as well; skip unless set

options.name: --report
options.help: A report file a full run writes: json (mutation.json), html (mutation.html) or sarif (mutation.sarif), in target/mutastic unless a path is given, or none; json and html unless set

options.name: --shard
options.help: Run only the Nth of M shares of the mutants, to split one run across machines. It keeps its results in shares/N-of-M in target/mutastic for --from-shards

options.name: --from-shards
options.help: Run no mutants: put together the results every share of a split run kept, found anywhere in DIR, as the whole run, with its reports and threshold

options.name: --format
options.help: How the result is shown; full on a terminal, concise elsewhere, agent for coding agents; explain takes full and jsonl

options.name: --vocabulary
options.help: plain says caught and missed; classic says killed and survived

options.name: --color
options.help: Colour: auto uses it on a terminal that wants it

options.name: --hyperlinks
options.help: File locations as links a terminal can open: auto uses them on a terminal

options.name: --progress
options.help: Progress on stderr: redrawn in place on a terminal, a line every 30 s in logs, CI and agents' runs, or none

options.name: --top
options.help: How many of the queue next shows, at most one a function and two a file; 1 unless set, at most 25

options.name: --reason
options.help: Why the mutant isn't worth a test: every ignore says

ignore.commandLine: mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --reason="totals are rounded to tens"
ignore.cargo: cargo mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --reason="totals are rounded to tens"

options.name: --as
options.help: What sort of decision it is

ignore.commandLine: mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --as=unreachable --reason="totals are rounded to tens"
ignore.cargo: cargo mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --as=unreachable --reason="totals are rounded to tens"

options.name: --remove
options.help: Take the mutant's ignore, or its proposal, away, so it runs again

options.name: --propose
options.help: Propose the ignore for a person to accept, rather than make it: a coding agent's way. An equivalent or unreachable mutant's reason says the one case where it differs and why that can't happen

ignore.commandLine: mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --propose --as=unreachable --reason="Differs only when total is 100. That can't happen because prices end in 9."
ignore.cargo: cargo mutastic ignore mb2f8ae57 --propose --as=unreachable --reason="Differs only when total is 100. That can't happen because prices end in 9."

options.name: --accept
options.help: Accept a proposed ignore: it moves into the ignores, as proposed

options.name: --prune
options.help: Take away every ignore whose line has changed; with baseline, every mutant the tests catch now

options.name: --hook
options.help: Run as the agent's hook: read its input on stdin, and answer as its hooks do

options.name: --tries
options.help: With --hook, how many times check sends the agent back before it lets it stop and says what's left, from 1 to 100; 3 unless set

options.name: --edition
options.help: Which edition runs; unless set, the build file in dir, or the nearest above it: Cargo.toml for rust, pom.xml, build.gradle or settings.gradle for java

environment.name: MUTASTIC_FORMAT
environment.meaning: The format when --format isn't given
environment.detail: For a machine or a CI job that always wants the same format, `concise` say.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_AGENT=1
environment.meaning: The agent format, for coding agents
environment.detail: Coding agents set it, so mutastic answers in the format they read best, with progress as lines. `MUTASTIC_FORMAT` still wins.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_VOCABULARY
environment.meaning: plain or classic, when --vocabulary isn't given
environment.detail: `classic` says killed and survived instead of caught and missed. The JSON report and the event stream always use the standard names.

environment.name: NO_COLOR
environment.meaning: No colour
environment.detail: Set to anything, it turns colour off, as it does for many tools.

environment.name: FORCE_COLOR
environment.meaning: Colour even off a terminal
environment.detail: Set to anything, it turns colour on where mutastic can't tell a person is reading, such as a CI log that shows colour. It wins over `NO_COLOR`.

environment.name: TERM=dumb
environment.meaning: No colour, unless `FORCE_COLOR` is set, and progress as lines

environment.name: MUTASTIC_PROGRESS
environment.meaning: auto, bar, counter or none, when --progress isn't given
environment.detail: For a Gradle or Maven build, or a CI job, that always wants the same.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_TERM_PROGRESS
environment.meaning: true or false: whether the terminal's tab shows the run's progress
environment.detail: Unset, it does in Windows Terminal, ConEmu, Ghostty and WezTerm, which say they draw it. Cargo's `CARGO_TERM_PROGRESS_TERM_INTEGRATION` is read too.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_HEARTBEAT
environment.meaning: Seconds a log may go without a progress line
environment.detail: 30 unless set. Off a terminal, a line with the phase, its counts and its clock is printed whenever this long has passed since the last.

environment.name: CI
environment.meaning: Progress as lines, not redrawn in place
environment.detail: Set to anything but `false` or `0`; as are `TF_BUILD`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI`, `BUILDKITE`, `JENKINS_URL`, `TEAMCITY_VERSION` and `CIRCLECI`, since some CI services pretend to be a terminal.

environment.name: CLAUDECODE
environment.meaning: Progress as lines, for a coding agent
environment.detail: As are `CLAUDE_CODE`, `GEMINI_CLI`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `OPENCODE`, `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `CURSOR_AGENT`, `REPL_ID`, `JUNIE_DATA`, `GOOSE_PROVIDER` and `AUGMENT_AGENT`, which coding agents set. Only progress changes: the format is still `--format`'s.

environment.name: CARGO
environment.meaning: The cargo mutastic runs
environment.detail: Cargo sets it for `cargo mutastic`; `cargo` on the `PATH` otherwise.

environment.name: RUSTC
environment.meaning: The rustc Cargo builds with, as for any Cargo build

environment.name: MUTASTIC_VERSION
environment.meaning: In a Maven or Gradle project, the Java edition's release to use
environment.detail: Such as `0.5.0`, fetched if it isn't kept. Unset, from 1.0.0 it's the newest release of this mutastic's own major and minor version.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_HOME
environment.meaning: Where the Java edition's releases are kept

environment.name: MUTASTIC_STDERR_TTY
environment.meaning: Whether stderr is a terminal, 1 or 0, for the Java edition
environment.detail: The JDK can't tell, so `mutastic` sets it when it runs the Java edition, unless it's set already.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_COLUMNS
environment.meaning: The terminal's width, for the Java edition
environment.detail: The JDK can't ask the terminal, so `mutastic` sets it when it runs the Java edition on a terminal, unless it's set already.

environment.name: MUTASTIC_JAVA_ENGINE
environment.meaning: A Java edition's `bin/mutastic` to run instead, such as one built from its source

environment.name: MUTASTIC_JAVA_RELEASES
environment.meaning: Where the Java edition's releases are downloaded from, for a mirror

environment.name: JAVA_HOME
environment.meaning: The JDK the Java edition runs on

exitCodes.meaning: The score reaches the threshold, or with --fail-on-new no miss is new; for verify, each mutant named is caught, skipped, or crashed where a crash proves nothing; for gate check, the task is done; for next, nothing missed is left but what's proposed for ignoring

The score is below the threshold, or with --fail-on-new a miss is new; for verify, a mutant named is still missed or not covered; for gate check, the task isn't done; for ignore --accept or --remove, the mutant isn't proposed or ignored; for next, something is queued; for baseline, there's one already, or none to prune

mutastic couldn't run: an unknown option, a word the command doesn't take, not a Cargo package, a workspace's root, a test that fails with no mutant in, an id that isn't a mutant of the package, shares --from-shards can't put together as one run, --fail-on-new with no baseline, or no task open for gate check
